why: APPEND-ONLY, WRITTEN BY A HUMAN, VERIFIED BY THE BUILD. `renames.json` refuses while an id has vanished from the library; `value-changes.json` refuses while a computed value has moved. This one refuses while a rule inside `scripts/build-indicator-manifest.mjs` withdraws an indicator the committed manifest is already offering. The exemption it replaces was reasoned — a rule the generator applied is not the rename-versus-removal ambiguity, because the reason is written, printed and in the diff — but it removed the only ratchet on catalogue size and nothing took its place: three ordinary indicators were withdrawn behind a new rule and 307 rows were written with `npm test`, `npm run e2e` and `npm run proof` all green, the single trace a stderr line nothing asserts. A host's saved workspace loses `bop` exactly as hard whether the id vanished or was withdrawn. The reason does not have to be invented here — the generator already printed it. It has to be SIGNED. Nothing is ever deleted from this list: it is how a reader knows what the catalogue has stopped offering and on whose word. AND IT CARRIES THE DIGEST THE ROW LEFT AT, because withdrawing an id is the one sanctioned command that removes it from the manifest AND its entry from `fingerprints.json` at once — which is exactly the shape `value-changes.json` reads as an indicator that never existed. Measured in two runs with nothing typed by hand: `wma` withdrawn on a signed sentence, then restored with its arithmetic multiplied by 1.0001, arrived as a debut — 310 offered, `--check` exit 0, the proof green, zero value declarations, a tampered digest on file. A row this list names is one the catalogue KNOWS and stopped offering, so it comes back answering for the value it left with.
form: Each entry is one indicator leaving the catalogue once: `id`, `reason` (why losing it is acceptable, in a sentence — not the generator's own rule restated), `measuredAt` (the vendor version the withdrawal was decided against), `values` (the digest the row was leaving at, which `scripts/build-indicator-manifest.mjs` prints in the refusal and checks against `fingerprints.json` before the entry is dropped), and `encoding` (the spelling that digest was taken under, as `fingerprints.json`'s own `algorithm.id`). A `reason` that is absent or empty does not count as a declaration, and a `values` that is absent, malformed or not the digest on file is refused on the run that would erase it.
